jobs:
  prepare:

      issues: write

    outputs:
      approved: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.approved }}
      issue_number: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Authenticate status callbacks
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
          import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';
          const env = process.env;
          const origin = env.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN.replace(/\/$/, '');
          const url = new URL(env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL);
          url.searchParams.set('audience', origin);
          async function json(url, options) {
            const response = await fetch(url, { ...options, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) });
            if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Callback authentication HTTP ${response.status}`);
            return response.json();
          }
          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 8; attempt++) {
            try {
              const identity = await json(url, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}` } });
              const { token } = await json(`${origin}/api/github/${env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${env.ISSUE_NUMBER}/callback-token`, {
                method: 'POST', headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${identity.value}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
                body: JSON.stringify({ run: env.GITHUB_RUN_ID, attempt: Number(env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT) })
              });
              console.log(`::add-mask::${token}`);
              appendFileSync(env.GITHUB_ENV, `OMGITHUB_CALLBACK_TOKEN=${token}\n`);
              break;
            } catch (error) {
              if (attempt === 7) throw error;
              await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, Math.min(20000, 3000 * 2 ** attempt)));
            }
          }
          NODE
      - name: Register preparation
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --retry 2 --retry-all-errors --max-time 15 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $OMGITHUB_CALLBACK_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data "{\"run\":\"$GITHUB_RUN_ID\",\"attempt\":$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT,\"sequence\":1,\"state\":\"starting\",\"phase\":\"initializing\"}" \
            "$OMGITHUB_ORIGIN/api/github/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$ISSUE_NUMBER/run"
      - name: Checkout trusted preparation code

      - name: Validate and claim issue request

Game concept: "Vanguard Ballistics: Tactical Operations" — landscape tactical top-down shooter. Need complete playable game with ballistics (bullet drop? ricochet? penetration?), tactical operations, gunsmith armory, campaign mode per manifest shortcuts. Should be polished and mobile-friendly.

Let me plan the game design deeply to make it fun and complete:

Genre: Top-down tactical shooter with realistic ballistics, cover, enemy AI, squad? Player controls a vanguard operator in procedurally generated/level-based missions. Aim with mouse/touch, shoot with trigger; movement WASD/left joystick. Weapons have recoil, spread, bullet velocity/travel time, penetration, ricochet, magazine/reload, grenades, dash. Enemies with vision cones, cover, patrol, alert states. Objectives: eliminate hostiles, secure intel, reach extraction. Campaign of ~6 operations with escalating difficulty. Gunsmith: unlock/upgrade weapons with credits. Persistence localStorage.

Given time constraints, aim for a single-file-ish or modular JS app with canvas 2D rendering, no dependencies. Must look great. Need screenshots via playwright.

Core features:
- Menu / mission select / armory / settings / how-to-play.
- Top-down 2.5D-ish visuals: dark tactical palette, grid floor, walls, crates, cover, fog of war/vision cones, muzzle flashes, tracers, bullet casings, blood/sparks, screen shake, lighting vignette, scanline, HUD.
- Player: health, armor, stamina/sprint, ammo, grenades, dash/roll maybe. Reload. Weapon switching between primary and sidearm.
- Aiming: mouse aim, click/hold fire; touch: dual sticks (left move, right aim/fire). Auto-fire when aim stick engaged, or dedicated fire button. Landscape orientation.
- Ballistics: projectiles with speed, drag, penetration through cover depending on material and weapon penetration; ricochet chance; bullet drop? Top-down, could simulate velocity and damage falloff; wall penetration with damage reduction. Bullet trails. Tracer.
- Enemy AI: patrol, investigate gunfire, take cover, flank, shoot bursts with telegraph (laser aim), grenades later. Different types: grunt, marksman (laser), heavy (shield), drone? Keep 3 types.
- Levels: tile-based map with walls, crates, sandbags, explosive barrels, extraction zone, intel. Multiple missions with handcrafted maps via procedural generation seeded.
- Objectives: eliminate all hostiles + reach extraction; some missions "recover intel" then extract. Timer? Credits reward based on accuracy, time, health.
- Campaign progression with mission unlock, difficulty.
- Gunsmith armory: buy weapons (SMG, rifle, shotgun, DMR, LMG), attachments/upgrades (scope, extended mag, suppressor, armor-piercing) with credits. Equip primary/secondary.
- Audio: WebAudio synthesized gunshots, ricochets, explosions, UI clicks, ambient. Mute toggle.
- Settings: audio, screen shake, aim assist? touch sensitivity.
- Pause menu, mission complete/failed screens, restart.
- Tutorial/help overlay.
- Save in localStorage.

Rendering: canvas at devicePixelRatio capped, fixed world camera follow with slight lookahead toward aim, zoom adaptive. Use offscreen canvas for static level? Simple draw.

We need robust collision: circle vs axis-aligned rectangles (walls, crates). Line of sight raycast vs rects. Bullets step with substeps and collide with rects (penetration: reduce damage/velocity per material, ricochet if angle shallow and material hard). Bullet vs actors circle collision along segment.

Maps: build from a grid string maybe 48x32 tiles with '#' walls, 'C' crates, 'S' sandbag (low cover? but top-down cover blocking LOS and bullets), 'B' barrel explosive, '.' floor. Spawn points. Use 32px tiles, world 1536x1024. Camera zoom ~0.9 on desktop.

Need mobile landscape, but also portrait phones? Manifest orientation landscape. We can show rotate prompt in portrait for phones? Better support portrait too? Tactical top-down with dual sticks works portrait; but request implies landscape. We'll design responsive: if portrait on phone, show "rotate device" overlay (and allow tap to continue?) Simpler: allow play in both, adapt camera. But safe: show rotate hint non-blocking. I'll support both, with HUD scaled. The game should fill viewport.

Implementation structure:
- index.html (menu DOM overlays, canvas)
- css/style.css
- js/audio.js, js/input.js, js/world.js? Might be simpler to modularize: main.js with all? Large file maybe 2500+ lines. Modular is cleaner: 
  - js/util.js (math, rng, storage)
  - js/audio.js
  - js/content.js (weapons, missions, upgrades)
  - js/entities.js (player, enemy, bullets, particles)
  - js/maps.js (level gen)
  - js/game.js (state, update, render)
  - js/ui.js (menus, HUD DOM)
  - js/main.js (bootstrap)
Need no build step; use ES modules. Static server default works.

Testing: playwright-cli. Need to serve with start.sh? Use tmux persistent server per Agents.md. Could use `python3 -m http.server 3000` or the default start (node default-start). Simpler: python http.server in tmux. But capture.sh expects port? The runtime default likely serves on APP_PORT=3000. We can use start.sh in tmux which runs node default-start; it watches. Let's do `tmux new -d -s serve 'bash start.sh'`. Then playwright-cli open http://localhost:3000 (or 3002? Agents.md mentions 3002 for Pascal). APP_PORT 3000. default-start probably uses 3000. Check default-start quickly.

Also the Android bundle: include assetlinks with host? Existing assetlinks probably generic. We'll copy all bundle files into repo root; but "well-known/assetlinks.json" should be `.well-known/assetlinks.json`. The zip uses "well-known" without dot perhaps because hidden. I'll preserve and maybe rename to `.well-known`. Also need PWA manifest and service worker for TWA to work. The TWA manifest references manifest.webmanifest and pwa icons at root.     speed: up.has('boots') ? 1.1 : 1,
    grenades: up.has('pouch') ? 5 : 3,
    focusCooldown: up.has('focus') ? 13 : 19,
    suppressed: up.has('suppressor'),
    armorPlates: up.has('armor'),
  };
}

export function resolveWeapon(id, save) {
  const base = WEAPONS[id] || WEAPONS.vector;
  const up = upgradeSet(save);
  const w = { ...base };
  if (up.has('ap')) {
    w.dmg = base.dmg * 1.08;

  if (up.has('optic')) w.spread = base.spread * 0.82;

    w.sound = 'suppressed';
  }
  w.reserve = Math.round(base.reserve * (up.has('mag') ? 1.25 : 1));

}
